title: Show session directory
description:
Add `session.directory` (fall back to `session.path`) to results.

- Human view: show the directory line (e.g. alongside slug).
- `--json`: expose a `directory` field.
- Implement now against the existing TS prototype.

Note: filtering/scoping by directory belongs to the search & scoping epic; this ticket is display-only.

Acceptance: directory shown in human + json for `cotails <term>` and `--title-only`.
notes:
Implemented in opencotails.ts:
- Added `directory` to both SELECTs (buildTitleQuery: `directory`; buildPartQuery: `s.directory AS directory`).
- renderHuman now shows `slug · directory` on the meta line (grey).
- `--json` exposes `directory` automatically (whole row is serialized).

Verified: human + --title-only + --json all surface the session directory (e.g. `/home/rektide/src/opencotails`).

title: Information gathering & display
description:
Surface the metadata, timeline, and lineage around opencode sessions so a user can orient on *what a session is and how it came to be* — not just whether it matches a search term.

Today `cotails` reports only `id`, `slug`, `title`, `updated`, and a text `snippet`. The opencode schema carries far richer signal that is currently invisible (all on the `session` table unless noted):

- **Provenance:** `time_created` (when it began), `directory` / `path` (where), `project_id` -> `project.name`.
- **Fork lineage:** `fork_session_id` + `fork_message_id` — the parent session and the exact message at which this session diverged.
- **Lifecycle:** `time_compacting`, `time_suspended`, `time_archived`.
- **Cost/usage:** `cost`, `tokens_input`, `tokens_output`, `tokens_reasoning`, `tokens_cache_read`/`write`.

This epic owns **reporting** — reading these fields and rendering them in both human and `--json` output. It does NOT own the matching/query side (search & scoping epic) or the FTS index (index epic).

## Scope (children)
- `cotail-created-at` — first `time_created`.
- `cotail-fork-time` — last fork time.
- `cotail-fork-point` — the previous prompt+reply and fork prompt+reply around the fork boundary, with timestamps.
- `cotail-directory` — the session directory (implement first).

## Out of scope
- Search semantics, scoping filters, FTS index, Rust port (separate epics).

title: Show last fork point (prev reply <-> fork reply, with timestamps)
description:
Given `session.fork_message_id` (the message at the divergence boundary), render the two turns flanking it:

- the **previous prompt + reply** immediately before the boundary, with its `time_created` stamp;
- the **fork prompt + reply** at/after the boundary, with its `time_created` stamp.

Fetch turns from `message`/`part` (v1) or `event` filtered to `message.part.updated.1` (v2) — see the README "V2 event fallback" section for the table/field mapping.

Acceptance: for a forked session, both boundary turns render with timestamps in human and json output.

title: Show last fork time
description:
A session forks via `session.fork_session_id` (parent) + `session.fork_message_id` (divergence point).

"Last fork time" = the most recent fork event touching this session. Two interpretations:
1. This session forked from its parent (its own `time_created` when `fork_session_id` is set).
2. A child forked FROM this session (`max(time_created)` over sessions where `fork_session_id = this.id`).

Decision needed: default to interpretation 2 (latest fork touching the session); show interpretation 1 when set.

Acceptance: fork time rendered (human + json) where fork lineage exists; omitted when none.

title: Show session first-created time
description:
Add `session.time_created` to results alongside the existing `updated` timestamp.

- Human view: distinguish created vs updated (show both compactly).
- `--json`: expose a `created` field.

Acceptance: first-created timestamp from `session.time_created` appears in both human and json output.
